text: Given graph_get_user is called with no select (the default profile) and the resolved user has no manager, When the Graph response has no manager key, Then the tool's returned JSON contains "manager": null, not an omitted key

Given graph_get_user is called with select=["proxyAddresses","manager"] and the resolved user has no manager, When the Graph response has no manager key, Then the tool returns {id, proxyAddresses, manager: null}

Given graph_get_user requests manager and the Graph response already has a populated manager object, When the tool returns, Then the manager object is unchanged (the null-injection never overwrites a real value) -- regression guard for the has-a-manager path

Given a user_id that resolves to a real user with no manager, When graph_remove_manager is called, Then it returns {user_id, removed: false, previous_manager: null, reason: no_manager} and the response specifically does NOT contain "status" or "group_id" keys -- regression-confirmation guard against the 2026-11-02 retest's reported (and unreproduced) {"status": "removed"} shape, which matches graph_remove_group_member, not this tool

Given graph_get_user is called with no select param, When the tool builds its request, Then the default $select includes onPremisesImmutableId, onPremisesSamAccountName, createdDateTime, and lastPasswordChangeDateTime -- regression-confirmation guard, same assertion as round 2/3's existing test_get_user_default_select_includes_onprem_and_audit_fields, named under this round in direct response to the 2026-11-02 retest's Issue C
